title: Assign the Standard Queue
subtitle: The quiet path still logs
scenario: Not every ticket is a P1. TKT-4002 is a P3 bug - it takes the standard path. Assign it to its routing-table queue and log the assignment, so the routine lane is as traceable as the escalation lane.
input: TKT-4002 (bug, P3): "The export button throws an error on one report." Not a P1, so it routes to its table queue: bug -> bug-queue. Assign it to bug-queue and log the assignment. The Queue Lead owns standard assignment.
instructions: Record which queue the ticket is assigned to (from the routing table).
Validate to mint the queue assignment record.

fields.label: Assigned queue
fields.explain: A bug routes to bug-queue per the routing table; incident-bridge is for outages, not standard bugs.

fields.label: Assigned by
fields.explain: The Queue Lead owns standard assignment; Tier-2 and the Duty Manager are for escalations, not routine routing.

fields.label: Assignment logged
fields.explain: Standard does not mean unlogged; the routine lane must be as auditable as escalation.

copilotPrompt: Capture a standard queue assignment for TKT-4002 (bug, P3): assigned queue bug-queue (from the routing table), assigned by the Queue Lead, logged yes. The quiet path still records where the ticket went.
successMessage: Ticket assigned to bug-queue and logged. The routine path is fully traceable.

sections.title: Most tickets are not P1
sections.body: The vast majority take the standard path. If only escalations are logged, most of the day's work is invisible - the routine lane needs the same record as the loud one.

sections.title: The table decides the queue
sections.body: A bug goes to bug-queue because the routing table says so, not because an agent felt like it. Sourcing the queue from config keeps assignment consistent.

sections.title: Log it anyway
sections.body: Recording who assigned it and when means the digest can count it and an auditor can trace it. Silence on the quiet path is how volume becomes a mystery.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A queue assignment record the SLA tracker and digest read, just like the escalation record.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd drop the ticket in its queue and log who did it, so the routine work is counted, not just the fires.

tools.powerAutomate: assign to the queue and write an assignment log row
tools.zapier: move the ticket to its queue and record it

takeaway.heading: Ticket assigned
points: You assigned TKT-4002 to bug-queue from the routing table.
The Queue Lead owns standard assignment, and it was logged.
The routine lane is as traceable as the escalation lane.
The SLA tracker and digest read this assignment record.
The workflow can now route and log standard tickets, not just P1s.
